Report_ID: Postoperative pain VAS (scale 1-10) at 6 h (day of surgery)
Title: Micropercutaneous nephrolithotomy (microperc) vs retrograde intrarenal surgery for the management of small renal calculi: a randomized controlled trial
Author: Sabnis RB, Ganesamoni R, Doshi A, Ganpule AP, Jagtap J, Desai MR
Comment: Group 1 is the microperc (PCNL-type) treatment arm and group 2 the RIRS control arm, matching the paper's own table column order; sign convention PCNL − RIRS = +1.0 VAS points. '±'/parenthetical values are SD per Methods ('reported as the number and percent or mean (SD) values'). M_diff left empty to avoid sign ambiguity; both means/SDs/Ns reported explicitly. Patients and outcome assessors were not blinded.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Microperc group (micro-PCNL, 4.85-F/16-gauge all-seeing needle with 272-mm holmium:YAG laser fibre)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: adults (age ≥18 years) with single renal stone or multiple stones in the same line <1.5 cm
Recruitment source: single tertiary care urological hospital, Nadiad, Gujarat, Western India (Feb 2011 - Aug 2012)
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) pain visual analogue score, scale 1-10, at 6 h postoperatively
Outcome variable: Postoperative pain VAS (scale 1-10) at 6 h (day of surgery)
outcome_family: postoperative pain VAS on the day of surgery (postoperative day 0)
effect_direction: positive (MD = +1.0 VAS points; more pain after micro-PCNL, favours RIRS)

Title: Super-mini percutaneous nephrolithotomy (SMP) versus retrograde intrarenal surgery for the treatment of 1-2 cm lower-pole renal calculi: an international multicenter randomized controlled trial
Author: Zeng et al.
Comment: M_diff = 0.9 computed as mean_SMP (4.1) − mean_RIRS (3.2), matching the paper's own reported 95% CI for this difference (0.344 to 1.365), so positive = more pain after PCNL. Per-arm n for the VAS rows is not explicitly stated; ITT randomized Ns (80 per arm) were used (77 received SMP and 76 received RIRS per protocol). Participant type: adults aged 18-70 years with a single 1-2 cm lower-pole renal calculus
Recruitment source: 10 academic medical centers (8 in China, 1 in India, 1 in Turkey)
Outcome measurement: Mean (SD) pain VAS score, range 1-10, at 6 h after surgery
Outcome variable: Postoperative pain VAS score at 6 h (day of surgery)
outcome_family: postoperative pain VAS on the day of surgery (postoperative day 0)
effect_direction: positive (MD = +0.9 VAS points; more pain after super-mini PCNL, favours RIRS)
